sections.title: Name and recognition
sections.text: Russula pseudodelica J.E. Lange is recorded as a current name by Index Fungorum (published in 1926). It is a large white to cream russula with a deeply depressed, eventually funnel-shaped cap that soon becomes dirty yellow and often holds soil debris. The gills are narrow, crowded and decurrent, sometimes forked or anastomosing; they become pale ochre. The stem is short, stout and white, sometimes greyish at the base. The flesh is white and may grey at the stem base; the spore deposit is pale ochre. Funga Nordica also notes a slightly acrid taste; this is not a reason to taste an unidentified mushroom.

sections.title: Habitat and taxonomic limits
sections.text: European descriptions report it in broadleaf woodland, including under beech, fruiting in autumn; it is rare in several regions. The field concept follows Lange’s Danish description as used in Funga Nordica. A 2025 molecular study and a recent European key discuss the interpretation of the name: R. pseudodelica may be the correct name for R. flavispora, but a Danish epitype is still needed. Index Fungorum records the current name without resolving that discussion; photographs cannot settle these difficult identifications.

sections.title: Caution
sections.text: Edibility is not established by the sources consulted. Do not consume a specimen identified from this entry or its image; similar white russulas may require microscopic or chemical examination to distinguish.

traits: Large white to cream russula, cap deeply depressed and eventually funnel-shaped
Narrow, crowded, decurrent gills, sometimes forked; cream then pale ochre
Short, stout, white stem; base may turn greyish
White flesh, sometimes greying at the stem base; cream to pale ochre spore deposit
Broadleaf woodland, beech reported; autumn in European sources
safetyNote: Edibility is not established in the sources consulted. Do not consume a specimen identified from this entry or illustration. Distinguishing it from similar white russulas may require specialist examination.
